tracks.legalName: Expungement of a conviction for conduct no longer prohibited, 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(1) and (b)
tracks.publicName: Expunge a conviction for something that is no longer a crime

controllingAuthority.summary: A person may petition the Criminal Division of the Superior Court for expungement where the person was convicted of an offence for which the underlying conduct is no longer prohibited by law or designated as a criminal offence. The court shall grant the petition where the person completed any sentence or supervision for the offence and any restitution and surcharges ordered by the court are paid in full, subject to the § 7282 surcharge waiver. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 7602(b) carries no waiting period and no interests-of-justice escape hatch — the contrast with the sealing subsections at (c), (d) and (e) is deliberate. After Act 60 of 2025, effective 2025-07-01, this is the only surviving expungement route in chapter 230; everything else that formerly led to expungement now leads to sealing. Section 7602(a)(5) disapplies the entire section to a commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder seeking to clear a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle.

exclusions: Any conviction where the underlying conduct is still prohibited or still designated as a criminal offence. The petitioner must prove decriminalisation; the offence being old is not enough.
A commercial driver's licence or commercial learner's permit holder seeking to clear a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle, under § 7602(a)(5), which disapplies the whole section.
Any case where restitution or surcharges ordered on any conviction remain unpaid, unless the surcharge was waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Section 7602(b) imposes no clock beyond completion of the sentence or supervision.
At least two years before another petition, unless the court authorises a shorter period (§ 7605).

geography.venue: The Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court (13 V.S.A. § 7601(1)), in the county that handled the case. Vermont has a unified Superior Court and one statewide Judiciary form set, with no county form variation identified.

components.notes: Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228, revision 04/2026, published by the Vermont Judiciary for the Vermont Superior Court and used in every division and county. It is a participant-completed application in support of a filing: not a petition, not a stipulation, not an order, not an outside-party document, and not a relief route of its own. It is included only where the participant asks the court to waive the filing fee, and never for a participant who pays it. The current object is the two-page, eighty-field AcroForm the Judiciary's own fee-waiver page and forms-library row serve at https://www.vtcourts.gov/media/47; the legacy static path /sites/default/files/documents/600-00228.pdf still returns HTTP 200 but carries the superseded 11/2019 revision with an incompatible 129-field structure and must not be bound. Identity settled by vt-600-00228-source-identity-resolution. Not needed on this track because no fee applies.

Explains that Vermont is now a sealing state and that this is the one surviving expungement route; that the participant must prove the conduct is no longer criminal, including the drug-amount showing for a regulated-drug possession conviction; that there is no filing fee; the stipulation path and that the prosecutor may refuse; that the respondent notifies any known victim under § 7608; that a pending charge anywhere freezes the petition; that a denial carries a two-year bar; and that expunged records may still appear in a federal background check.

participantInputs.question: Which county handled the case?
What is the docket number? A separate petition is needed for each unrelated offence and for each county.
What exactly were you convicted of — the offence name and, if you have it, the statute section? Vermont's qualifying-crime screen runs on the exact section, not the offence label.
On what date did you finish all the terms and conditions of the sentence?
Have you paid in full all restitution and surcharges ordered for any crime you have ever been convicted of — not only this one?
Did the court waive any surcharge under 13 V.S.A. § 7282?
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked only where a surcharge is outstanding, because a § 7282 waiver excuses it.

participantInputs.question: Do you have any criminal charge pending anywhere right now?
Do you hold a commercial driver's licence or commercial learner's permit, and was this offence committed in a motor vehicle?
Has a court ever denied a petition to seal or expunge this record? If so, when?
Before you file, do you want to ask the prosecutor's office to agree to this in writing? If they agree, the judge decides on the papers with no hearing.
Why is the conduct you were convicted of no longer a crime? Name the change in the law if you know it.
If this was a regulated-drug possession conviction, how much was involved? The amount decides whether the conduct is still prohibited.
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked only on a regulated-drug possession conviction, because the Judiciary's filing guide requires the petitioner to prove the amount is no longer prohibited or has had criminal sanctions removed.

rules.filing: Filed with the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court in the county that handled the case. Offences arising from the same incident or occurrence may go on one petition. Offences not related to the same incident, or offences in more than one county, require a separate petition for each offence. That is a per-offence cost and packet multiplier, not a per-county one.
rules.fees: No filing fee. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e) the $90 fee applies only to a motion to seal a criminal history record of a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a), and expressly does not apply to any other motion to seal or expunge under 13 V.S.A. § 7602, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) or other records-clearance provisions.
rules.feeWaiver: Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228 (revision 04/2026), the Vermont Judiciary's single statewide fee-waiver application. Use it only if you are asking the court to waive the filing fee; if you are paying the fee, you do not need it. It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page.
rules.notice: The court notifies the prosecuting office. Under § 7608 the respondent, not the participant and not the court, must give notice of the petition to any victim of the offence known to the respondent, and the victim has the right to offer a statement to the respondent before any stipulation or to offer one to the court. The respondent's inability to locate a victim after reasonable effort — first-class mail, telephone and email to the last known contact details — is not a bar to granting the petition.
rules.service: The participant does not serve the prosecutor with process. Where a stipulation is used, the Judiciary directs the participant to take or send the stipulation form to the prosecutor and to ask whether the prosecutor will file it or return it signed for the participant to file. Under § 7602(a)(4) the respondent files the stipulation.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. On a stipulation form the petitioner signs and the State's Attorney signs separately; LegalEase neither obtains nor asserts the prosecutor's signature.
rules.notarization: Not required by chapter 230 or by the Judiciary's published petition forms.

selfHelpStopConditions: The prosecutor opposes the petition, or the court schedules a hearing.
A victim files a statement in opposition. Under § 7608 the respondent must notify any known victim at the time the petition is filed, and the victim may offer a statement before any stipulation.
Any criminal charge is pending anywhere. Under § 7604 the court cannot act on the petition until the new charge is disposed of.
The criminal history record mixes qualifying and nonqualifying offences.

The participant holds a commercial driver's licence or commercial learner's permit and the offence was committed in a motor vehicle. Section 7602(a)(5) disapplies the whole section, not only the DUI route.
The offence may be a listed crime under 13 V.S.A. § 5301(7).
Any felony not plainly on the § 7601(4)(B) list.
Immigration consequences.
The participant wants to attack the underlying conviction rather than clear the record.
The participant cannot establish from a documented source that the conduct is no longer prohibited. "Old marijuana" is not enough.
The conviction is a regulated-drug possession offence and the amount involved is not established.

tracks.legalName: Expungement on discharge from a deferred sentence, 13 V.S.A. § 7041(e)
tracks.publicName: Records cleared after completing a deferred sentence

controllingAuthority.summary: On fulfilment of the terms of probation and of the deferred sentence agreement, the court shall strike the adjudication of guilt and discharge the person. Except as provided in subsection (h), the record of the criminal proceedings shall be expunged on discharge from probation, absent a finding of good cause by the court, and the court shall issue an order to expunge all records and files related to the arrest, citation, investigation, charge, adjudication of guilt, criminal proceedings and probation. Copies go to each agency, department or official named, and thereafter the court, law enforcement officers, agencies and departments reply that no record exists. Notwithstanding the subsection, the record is not expunged until restitution has been paid in full. Read at source on 2026-08-06: § 7041 sits in chapter 221, was not amended by Act 60, and its relief is court-driven — no petition is required and the participant files nothing to obtain it. Subsection (h) requires VCIC to retain a confidential special index of deferred sentences for sex offences requiring registration, accessible only by the VCIC director and one designated staff person for presentence investigation purposes.

exclusions: Any deferred sentence not yet fulfilled, or probation not yet discharged.
Any case where restitution has not been paid in full. The statute bars expungement until it is.
A sex offence requiring registration, to the extent of the § 7041(h) confidential VCIC special index, which survives the expungement.
Cases for which deferred adjudication is unavailable, including certain serious sexual offences against children, which forecloses this route entirely.
A court finding of good cause against expungement.

waitingPeriods.duration: Discharge from probation on fulfilment of the terms of probation and of the deferred sentence agreement. There is no separate waiting period.
The record is not expunged until restitution has been paid in full, however long that takes.

units.label: The expungement the court owes on discharge, and how to verify it happened
units.description: The ordinary and intended path. Section 7041(e) makes expungement the court's duty on discharge from probation, absent a finding of good cause, and nothing is filed by the participant. LegalEase confirms that the person was discharged and the adjudication of guilt struck, confirms restitution is paid in full, and explains how to check whether the expungement order issued. Anyone who completed a deferred sentence should not be sold a petition packet, and this unit is why.

units.label: Written request to the court where the expungement order did not issue
units.description: Applies only where the person was discharged, restitution is paid, and the order nevertheless did not issue. LegalEase generates a controlled written request to the Criminal Division of the Superior Court that entered the deferred sentence, identifying the docket, stating the date of discharge and the date restitution was satisfied, citing § 7041(e), and asking the court to enter the expungement order the statute requires absent a finding of good cause. There is no Judiciary form for this request; the statute supplies the destination, the court, the operative facts and the relief, which is what makes a controlled pleading supportable rather than a guess.

geography.venue: The Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court that entered the deferred sentence and discharged the person from probation.

destination.name: The Criminal Division of the Superior Court that entered the deferred sentence
destination.detail: On the ordinary path the court acts on its own on discharge and the participant submits nothing. Where the order did not issue, the written request goes back to the same court. The court sends copies of the order to each agency, department or official named in it.

The composition is alternative rather than sequential because exactly one unit applies and the units are not steps toward each other: either the court did what § 7041(e) requires, in which case the participant needs verification and nothing else, or it did not, in which case the participant sends a written request. That is the same shape counsel adopted for the no-conviction merge, where an automatic-sealing-and-verification unit stands alongside petition units, and it is applied consistently here. controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of a qualifying misdemeanour, or of qualifying misdemeanours arising out of the same incident or occurrence, may petition the Criminal Division of the Superior Court for sealing. Under § 7601(4)(A), read at source on 2026-08-06, a qualifying crime means all misdemeanour offences except sixteen enumerated exclusions, the first of which is a listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301(7). The waiting period is at least three years since the date the person completed the terms and conditions of the sentence. Restitution and surcharges ordered for any crime of which the person has been convicted must be paid in full, subject to the § 7282 waiver. The merits condition is drafted against the State: the court shall grant where the respondent has failed to show that sealing would be contrary to the interests of justice. Where the petitioner and the respondent stipulate, § 7602(a)(4) requires the court to grant the petition without hearing.

exclusions: A listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301(7). This cross-reference is the whole misdemeanour screen and must be encoded in full rather than paraphrased.
Sexual exploitation of children under chapter 64.
Violation of an abuse prevention order, an order against stalking or sexual assault, or a protective order concerning contact with a child under § 1030.
Abuse, neglect and exploitation of a vulnerable adult under chapter 28.
Voyeurism under § 2605(b) or (c).
Cruelty to animals under § 352(1) through (10).
Failure to comply with sex offender registry requirements under § 5409.
Hate-motivated crimes under § 1455.
Cruelty to a child under § 1304(a).
Cruelty by a person having custody of another under § 1305.
Mistreatment of persons with impaired cognitive function under § 1306.
Female genital mutilation under § 3151.
Sexual exploitation of a minor under § 3258(b).
Violation of an extreme risk protection order under § 4058(b)(1).
An offence committed in a motor vehicle as defined in 23 V.S.A. § 4 by a commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder.
Any offence requiring sex offender registration under chapter 167, subchapter 3.
A commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder seeking to seal a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle, under § 7602(a)(5), which disapplies the whole section.
Any case where restitution or surcharges on any conviction remain unpaid, unless waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.

rules.filing: Filed with the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court in the county that handled the case. Offences arising from the same incident or occurrence may go on one petition. Offences not related to the same incident, or offences in more than one county, require a separate petition for each offence. That is a per-offence cost and packet multiplier, not a per-county one.
rules.fees: No filing fee. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e) the $90 fee applies only to a motion to seal a criminal history record of a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a), and expressly does not apply to any other motion to seal or expunge under 13 V.S.A. § 7602, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) or other records-clearance provisions.
rules.feeWaiver: Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228 (revision 04/2026), the Vermont Judiciary's single statewide fee-waiver application. Use it only if you are asking the court to waive the filing fee; if you are paying the fee, you do not need it. It supports whatever you are already filing and is not a separate request to seal or expunge anything, so it does not change what you are asking the court to do. The packet names the form by its number and title and links the Judiciary's current fee-waiver page.
rules.notice: The court notifies the prosecuting office. Under § 7608 the respondent, not the participant and not the court, must give notice of the petition to any victim of the offence known to the respondent, and the victim has the right to offer a statement to the respondent before any stipulation or to offer one to the court. The respondent's inability to locate a victim after reasonable effort — first-class mail, telephone and email to the last known contact details — is not a bar to granting the petition.
rules.service: The participant does not serve the prosecutor with process. Where a stipulation is used, the Judiciary directs the participant to take or send the stipulation form to the prosecutor and to ask whether the prosecutor will file it or return it signed for the participant to file. Under § 7602(a)(4) the respondent files the stipulation.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. On a stipulation form the petitioner signs and the State's Attorney signs separately; LegalEase neither obtains nor asserts the prosecutor's signature.
rules.notarization: Not required by chapter 230 or by the Judiciary's published petition forms.

controllingAuthority.summary: A qualifying DUI misdemeanour may be sealed at least ten years after completion of the terms and conditions of the sentence, and only where the person is not the holder of a commercial driver's licence or commercial driver's permit under 23 V.S.A. chapter 39. The commercial-licence bar reaches further than this track: § 7601(4)(A)(xv) excludes from the qualifying-crime definition any offence committed in a motor vehicle by a commercial licence or permit holder, and § 7602(a)(5) disapplies the entire section to such a holder seeking to seal a misdemeanour or felony committed in a motor vehicle. A DUI committed before age 25 should be tested against the 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) route first, and a DUI committed at 18 to 21 against § 7609, since both beat the ten-year clock by a wide margin.

exclusions: A person who holds a commercial driver's licence or commercial driver's permit under 23 V.S.A. chapter 39. This is an express condition of § 7602(e) and is separately reinforced by § 7601(4)(A)(xv) and § 7602(a)(5).
Any case where restitution or surcharges on any conviction remain unpaid, unless waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.
A record mixing qualifying and nonqualifying offences, where the participant is being routed to § 7609 instead.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read in full at source on 2026-08-06. Section 7603 provides one remedy — sealing — reachable by three distinct routes, and Act 60 repealed subsections (c), (d), (e), (f) and (h), so no expungement route survives on a no-conviction record. Under (a)(1), unless either party objects in the interests of justice, the court shall issue a sealing order within 60 days after final disposition if the court did not make a probable cause determination at arraignment, the charge was dismissed before trial with or without prejudice, or the defendant was acquitted; nothing is filed and the duty runs to the court. Under (a)(2) the court may seal at any time if the prosecuting attorney and the defendant stipulate. Under (g) a person may petition at any time, and the court shall grant and issue the order if it finds that sealing serves the interests of justice or if the parties stipulate. Under (b), where a party objects the court schedules a hearing, and the defendant and the prosecuting attorney are the only parties. The burden on the (g) route is affirmative on the petitioner, unlike the § 7602 conviction tracks where the respondent must show the contrary.

exclusions: Any case that ended in a conviction, which routes to the § 7602 tracks instead.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere. Under § 7604 the court shall not act until the new charge is disposed of.

Expungement. Act 60 repealed § 7603(e), (f) and (h), so a no-conviction record can be sealed but not expunged, and automatic conversion of a sealed record to an expunged record after eight years no longer exists.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: This is the merge the adopted counsel crosswalk directs, and current authority confirms it is the right shape rather than merely the directed one. Section 7603, read in full at source on 2026-08-06, creates one remedy — sealing — with three routes to it: the court's own duty within 60 days under (a)(1), a stipulated grant at any time under (a)(2), and an ordinary petition at any time under (g). They are alternatives in the strict sense the schema means: exactly one applies, selection is by participant facts, and they are not steps toward each other. VT-SEAL-05, VT-SEAL-06 and VT-SEAL-07 are therefore three units of one composed mechanism and not three relief tracks, which is why fourteen source slots produce eleven tracks. Unit one is process_guidance on the substantive ground that no participant submission exists on the automatic route — the duty runs to the court and there is no petition, form, fee or application step — and not because a form is missing. Units two and three are official_pdf_fill on the current statewide petition. The burden difference between the routes is preserved rather than flattened: on § 7603(g) the petitioner must satisfy the court that sealing serves the interests of justice, which is the opposite posture from the § 7602 conviction tracks, and that statement is a participant-authored field with prompts. The Act 60 repeal of the no-conviction expungement routes is stated plainly, because a participant working from an older Vermont packet will look for relief that no longer exists.

limitations.statement: After 2025-07-01 Vermont is a sealing state, not an expungement state. Participant-facing copy must not use expungement as the umbrella term: expungement removes records from any accessible database and destroys the paper file, sealing moves them into a confidential file without destroying them, and after Act 60 expungement survives only for conduct that is no longer criminal.

tracks.publicName: Seal a record from when you were 18 to 21

controllingAuthority.summary: A person who was 18 to 21 years of age at the time they committed a qualifying crime may petition the Criminal Division of the Superior Court for sealing 30 days after completing the terms and conditions of the sentence. Read at source on 2026-08-06: the section heading and the operative text both fix the band at 18 to 21, and § 7609 contains no reference to age 25 anywhere. The conditions are that restitution and surcharges ordered for any crime of which the person has been convicted are paid in full, subject to the § 7282 waiver, and that the respondent has failed to show that sealing would be contrary to the interests of justice. Subsection (b)(1) is a hard bar: a criminal history record that includes both qualifying and nonqualifying offences is not eligible for sealing under this section. Order, notice and effect comply with § 7607(a) and (b). This is Vermont's fastest route by a wide margin, thirty days against three, seven or ten years, so the age question must be asked of every participant regardless of what else they say.

exclusions: A criminal history record that includes both qualifying and nonqualifying offences. Section 7609(b)(1) makes this an absolute bar, and it is the condition that most often closes this route.

An offence committed outside the 18 to 21 age band. A person under 18 falls outside chapter 230 entirely; a person over 21 runs on the ordinary § 7602 clocks, and an offence committed before age 25 should be tested against 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g).
Any offence that is not a qualifying crime under § 7601(4).
A commercial driver's licence or commercial permit holder seeking to seal an offence committed in a motor vehicle.
Any case where restitution or surcharges on any conviction remain unpaid, unless waived under § 7282.
Any case where a criminal charge is pending anywhere, under § 7604.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06. On application of a person who has pleaded guilty to or been convicted of a crime under Vermont law committed prior to attaining 25 years of age, or on the motion of the court having jurisdiction, and after notice to all parties of record and hearing, the court shall order the sealing of all files and records related to the proceeding if it finds that two years have elapsed since the final discharge of the person; that the person has not been convicted of a listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301 or adjudicated delinquent for such an offence for ten years prior to the application or motion, and no new proceeding is pending seeking such a conviction or adjudication; and that the person's rehabilitation has been attained to the satisfaction of the court. Subsection (m) bars sealing where restitution and surcharges are owed. Subsection (k) provides that the court shall provide assistance to persons who seek to file an application for sealing under the section. This provision sits outside chapter 230, was not amended by Act 60, and is procedurally unlike anything in that chapter: it uses an application rather than a petition, it is dual-initiated, it mandates notice to all parties of record and a hearing, it runs on a two-year clock from final discharge, and it places an affirmative rehabilitation burden on the participant. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e) no filing fee applies to a § 5119(g) motion.

exclusions: Any offence committed on or after the person attained 25 years of age.
A person convicted of a listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301, or adjudicated delinquent for such an offence, within the ten years prior to the application or motion.
A person with a new proceeding pending seeking such a conviction or adjudication.
A case where fewer than two years have elapsed since final discharge.
A case where restitution or surcharges remain owed, under § 5119(m).
A case where the court is not satisfied that rehabilitation has been attained. This is an affirmative burden on the participant and is unlike the burden allocation in chapter 230.

waitingPeriods.duration: Two years must have elapsed since the final discharge of the person.
No conviction for, or delinquency adjudication for, a listed crime as defined in 13 V.S.A. § 5301 for the ten years prior to the application or motion, and no such proceeding pending.

The Vermont Judiciary publishes no form for this application, and none was located on 2026-08-06; the statute supplies the court, the vehicle, the findings the court must make and the relief, which is what makes a controlled pleading supportable rather than a guess.

Prompts the participant to describe, in their own words and with their own documents, what they have done since final discharge. LegalEase never generates a rehabilitation argument and never asserts that rehabilitation has been attained; the court decides that to its own satisfaction.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06. controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06. Section 7601(4)(B)(iv) makes any offence for which the person has been granted an unconditional pardon from the Governor a qualifying felony. The pardon therefore changes the offence's status rather than its disposition, and it leads to sealing rather than expungement. Because the pardon route sits in the qualifying-felony subsection, the seven-year clock at § 7602(d) appears to apply even to a pardoned misdemeanour; whether a pardoned misdemeanour instead runs on the three-year clock at § 7602(c) is not resolved by the text. A pardon is not itself record relief in Vermont: it makes the offence a qualifying crime for sealing, and the sealing petition is still required.

rules.filing: Filed with the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court in the county that handled the case. Offences arising from the same incident or occurrence may go on one petition. Offences not related to the same incident, or offences in more than one county, require a separate petition for each offence. That is a per-offence cost and packet multiplier, not a per-county one.

rules.feeWaiver: Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs, form 600-00228 (revision 04/2026), the Vermont Judiciary's single statewide fee-waiver application. Use it only if you are asking the court to waive the filing fee; if you are paying the fee, you do not need it. rules.notice: The court notifies the prosecuting office. Under § 7608 the respondent, not the participant and not the court, must give notice of the petition to any victim of the offence known to the respondent, and the victim has the right to offer a statement to the respondent before any stipulation or to offer one to the court. The respondent's inability to locate a victim after reasonable effort — first-class mail, telephone and email to the last known contact details — is not a bar to granting the petition.
rules.service: The participant does not serve the prosecutor with process. Where a stipulation is used, the Judiciary directs the participant to take or send the stipulation form to the prosecutor and to ask whether the prosecutor will file it or return it signed for the participant to file.
